K-means seed generation from point coordinates

Source: R/seeding.R
voronoi_seeds_kmeans.Rd

Places k seed points at k-means cluster centres of the observed coordinates, so seeds (and the Voronoi cells built from them) follow the sampling density: clusters of observations attract seeds, empty ground gets none. Reach for this when you want cells that follow the data, so that counts per cell vary far less than on a fixed grid over clustered points (the density kind, the default, evens them out once there are more cells than clusters of points; plain k-means, partition = "kmeans", minimises the spread of points around each centre and does not equalise them), which is what keeps per-cell aggregates in summarize_by_cell() from resting on one or two observations. Use voronoi_seeds_random() instead when you want coverage of the study area rather than of the data, and get_voronoi_seeds() to pick between them by name.

Usage

voronoi_seeds_kmeans(
  points_sf,
  k,
  set_seed = 456,
  nstart = NULL,
  partition = c("density", "kmeans"),
  init = NULL,
  density_power = 1,
  density_k = 8,
  iter_max = NULL
)

Arguments

points_sf

An sf object with POINT geometries.

k

Integer; requested number of clusters, treated as an upper bound only. It is clamped, with a warning, to whichever is smaller of the number of distinct point positions and nrow(points_sf) - 1, because k-means can produce neither more centres than there are distinct points nor as many centres as there are rows. Check nrow() on the result. A select_resolution() result or a resolution_profile() is also accepted: its scored centres are returned when it carries them, whatever partition, init and density settings the call names (see n in get_voronoi_seeds() for which arguments a call is taken to name), and otherwise its count is used. A profile is read as get_voronoi_seeds() reads one passed as n: by cp when it was built without an estimate, and by select_resolution(criterion = "auto") when it was built with one (a size for pooled values, the lowest leave-one-out error for plain means). Such a count raises the warnings and the error described under n in get_voronoi_seeds() (classes "spatialkit_bound_chosen", "spatialkit_no_structure" and "spatialkit_no_default_criterion").

set_seed

Optional integer RNG seed. Default 456, so a call gives the same seeds every time whatever the session's random-number state; an outer set.seed() does not change them, and the caller's random-number stream is left as it was. Pass NULL to draw the k-means starts from the session's stream instead (the default of get_voronoi_seeds()).

nstart

The number of starts, of which the best is kept. NULL (default) is the kind's own number: 3 for partition = "density" and 10 for partition = "kmeans", the default of earlier versions. A number is run under either kind and either init: nstart = 10 gives the density kind the starts it had when 10 was the default.

partition

What the seeds minimise. "density" (default): the sum of squared distances from the points to their nearest seed, each point weighted by its local density to the power density_power; compact cells that, at the default power, hold about the same number of points each once k is above the number of dense places, and counts about as uneven as "kmeans" gives below that. "kmeans": the same sum unweighted; compact cells whose counts are several times higher in dense places than in sparse ones. It is the run of earlier versions, whose default it was: stats::kmeans() from 10 random starts on the rows as they come. Without the 'FNN' package the density kind finds its weights by comparing every pair of distinct locations, so its time grows with the square of their number; the seeds are the same, and nothing stops the call. See "Details".

init

How each start is drawn: "random" (k distinct locations at random, as stats::kmeans() draws them) or "kmeans++" (the seeds one at a time, each in proportion to its squared distance from those already drawn, times its weight under partition = "density"). NULL (default) is each kind's own rule: "random" for partition = "kmeans", the run this function has always made, and "kmeans++" for partition = "density". Under partition = "kmeans" from random starts the points are clustered in the order their rows come in; with init = "kmeans++", and under partition = "density", the rows are put in coordinate order first, so the seeds do not depend on their order.

density_power

For partition = "density": the power the local density is raised to for a point's weight, from 0 to 2. Default 1, which evens out the cell counts once the cells outnumber the dense places; 0 weights every point alike, and values above 1 give the cells of dense places fewer points than those of sparse places. Setting it under partition = "kmeans" is a warning.

density_k

For partition = "density": the number of nearest neighbours the local density is read from. Default 8.

iter_max

The most iterations a start runs for: a single positive whole number, or NULL (default) for the kind's own limit, 50 for partition = "kmeans" and 100 steps of Lloyd's iteration for partition = "density". Under partition = "density", and with init = "kmeans++", a kept start that was cut off at the limit is a warning of class "spatialkit_not_converged"; partition = "kmeans" from random starts keeps the warning stats::kmeans() gives.

Value

An sf object of at most k cluster-centre POINTs (fewer when k exceeds the number of distinct positions), with seed_id and method = "kmeans" columns matching get_voronoi_seeds(), and attr(, "cover"), the convex hull of points_sf (an sfc in its CRS). Seeds placed with partition = "density" or init = "kmeans++", and the scored centres of a profile of the density kind or from random starts, also carry attr(, "partition"): a list with kind, init, density_power and density_k, and for seeds this call placed iter, iter_max and converged (the iterations the kept start took, the limit, and whether it stopped before the limit). build_tessellation() returns the list as params$partition. Seeds with no such record are plain k-means: from random starts when this call placed them, or the scored centres of a k-means profile from k-means++ starts. When k is a select_resolution() result that carries count_rule, or a profile built with an estimate, the seeds carry that record as attr(, "count_rule"), with scored_cells TRUE for the scored centres and FALSE for centres this call fits itself at that count (see get_voronoi_seeds()).

Details

Lon/lat input is projected first so the k-means distances are metric and not degrees; so is input with no CRS whose coordinates look like lon/lat (the heuristic ensure_projected() applies, with its warning), and the seeds come back in the input's own coordinates. Rows with empty or non-finite coordinates are dropped with a warning, and k is clamped to the number of distinct positions.

A count given as a number gets a fresh partition, which is not the partition resolution_profile() or determine_optimal_levels() scored that count on: those fit their own run, the profile to every row or to a subsample, and keep the best of their own starts. Pass the select_resolution() result or the profile itself as k to get the scored one: the centres of the scored partition are then returned (in the CRS of points_sf, with attr(, "n_from")), and no k-means is run.

partition says what the seeds minimise. "kmeans" is the sum of squared distances from the points to their nearest seed, from nstart random starts by stats::kmeans() (Hartigan-Wong) unless init says otherwise; it was the default of earlier versions. The seeds follow the square root of the point density, so the cells are compact, smaller where the points are dense, and a cell in a dense place still holds several times the points of a cell in a sparse place. "density" weights each point by its local density (the number of points in the disc that reaches its density_k-th nearest neighbour, over the disc's area) to the power density_power, and is the default. At the default power of 1 the seeds follow the point density itself, and the cells are compact: many small cells where the points are dense, a few large ones where they are sparse. They hold about the same number of points each once k is above the number of dense places (clusters of points). With fewer cells than that a cell takes in whole clusters, large and small, and the counts are about as uneven as under "kmeans". The density kind is the best of nstart starts, each refined by at most 100 steps of Lloyd's iteration (iter_max sets another limit, and a kept start that was cut off at the limit is a warning of class "spatialkit_not_converged"); it does not depend on the order of the rows or on the unit of the coordinates, and points at one location share a cell. A seed can end with no point at counts from about a fifth of the points up, mostly from init = "random"; that is a warning of class "spatialkit_empty_cells". "The partition" in resolution_profile() gives the details and a simulated comparison of the two kinds.

The centres lie inside the points, so their own hull is smaller than the data's. The result carries the convex hull of points_sf as attr(, "cover"), and build_tessellation() clips the cells to that hull (grown by 2 percent of its diagonal) when no boundary is passed, so every point of points_sf falls in a cell.

See also

Other tessellation: build_tessellation(), create_grid_polygons(), create_grid_polygons_cached(), create_voronoi_polygons(), ensure_stable_poly_id(), get_voronoi_seeds(), plot_tessellation_map(), voronoi_seeds_random()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(100, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(100, 0, 1000)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
seeds <- voronoi_seeds_kmeans(pts, k = 8)   # density-weighted, 3 starts
nrow(seeds)   # at most 8: one seed per non-empty cluster
#> [1] 8
seeds         # the cluster centres, as an sf POINT layer in the points' CRS
#> Simple feature collection with 8 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 500197.6 ymin: 5000135 xmax: 500802.6 ymax: 5000911
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 32N
#>                   geometry seed_id method
#> 1 POINT (500596.5 5000605)       1 kmeans
#> 2 POINT (500371.1 5000409)       2 kmeans
#> 3 POINT (500802.6 5000255)       3 kmeans
#> 4 POINT (500316.8 5000797)       4 kmeans
#> 5 POINT (500197.6 5000577)       5 kmeans
#> 6   POINT (500799 5000911)       6 kmeans
#> 7 POINT (500785.6 5000620)       7 kmeans
#> 8 POINT (500513.3 5000135)       8 kmeans
# The k-means seeds of earlier versions: 10 random starts.
voronoi_seeds_kmeans(pts, k = 8, partition = "kmeans")
#> Simple feature collection with 8 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
